Peter — attaching an updated MAP (sheet 2 has the perf plan) and a short summary of the results we ran against your staging cluster last week. Key callouts first:

- Observed TTFT median at 420ms vs your targeted 250ms for the 512-token baseline.
- Sustained concurrency (50 clients, 8 requests/sec each) produced tail latency spikes above 1.2s at 95th pct.
- Throughput numbers were consistent with our Dedicated config, but your cluster shows variability at ~30–40% utilization.

Attachments: RD-9874_MAP_v2.xlsx (MAP with milestones and perf sheets)

Proposed next steps in MAP sheet:
1) Shared reproduction exercise — FinEdge runs client-side harness + we run server-side capture.
2) Small N experiments to isolate sequence-length and batching effects (2 days).
3) If mismatch persists, schedule a joint kernel/quantization debug session (we can loop in runtime).

If this aligns, we’ll add the explicit experiment matrix to the MAP and mark the 2-week close runway for the commercial milestone.

Jonas
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Thanks Jonas — got the MAP and the numbers. We ran a quick internal repro (attached logs) and saw similar TTFT medians (~430ms) but our 95th is even higher (1.35s). A few notes from our side:

- We are using client batching with a 128-token prefetch window; your test harness used single-request mode.
- We observed occasional long tails coincident with GC spikes on our side (Node.js worker pool).
- Sequence lengths in our workload average 600 tokens (longer than the 512 baseline).

Attaching: finedge_client_perf_logs.tar.gz (compressed logs + perf traces)

We want to close the MAP by the end of the month — can your team help triage the tooling differences (client batching and sequence lengths) and agree on an experiment matrix?

—Peter
Head of Platform
FinEdge AI

Quick findings after a first pass through their logs and our data:

1) Client batching and different request shapes are the top suspect — their 128-token prefetch + variable sequence length means more attention work per request; our baseline was optimized for 512 fixed-length runs.

2) Quantization variant mismatch: FinEdge is using a 4-bit hybrid quant build we did not run in the last test set; kernel selection falls back to less-optimized paths at certain sequence lengths, which explains the 95th tail.

3) Node-side GC spikes look like a valid secondary contributor. Recommend we: 
   - Short-term: Add client-side rate smoothing and recommend reducing prefetch to 64 tokens for initial runs; enable prefix/KV caching TTL = 30s in their harness.
   - Mid-term: Run a specific hybrid-quant canonical test on our infra (same model binary/quant flags) to directly compare. I can author the runbook.

Neha’s harness will be critical — if mode (B) reproduces their numbers in our infra, we can narrow the issue to runtime/quant/sequence interplay. If not, it’s likely an infra-level difference on FinEdge (GC, network).

Action items I’ll take now:
- Draft experiment-runbook.md (expected results, measurement hooks, log collection points).
- Schedule 2x 2-hour windows tomorrow for joint runs (block 10–12 and 15–17 PT).

Karthik
Senior Runtime Engineer
Redwood Inference
